title: Review: The motor effect; Induced potential, transformers and the National Grid (physics only) (HT only); Solar system; stability of orbital motions; satellites (physics only)
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Physics (8463) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.8.1-c18, 4.8.1-c07, 4.7.2-c05, 4.7.2-c12. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Supernova
items.clue: The explosion of a massive star.

items.label: Nebula
items.clue: A cloud of dust and gas in space.

items.label: Solenoid
items.clue: A wire wound into a long coil of many turns.

items.label: Electromagnetic relay
items.clue: A small current in a coil switches a separate circuit on or off.

questions.stem: The direction of the current in a straight wire is reversed. What happens to the magnetic field pattern?

options.text: The pattern and the arrows on it are both completely unchanged
The circles turn into straight lines pointing back along the wire
The circles stay, but the arrows point the other way round
The circles are replaced by a bar-magnet pattern with swapped poles

questions.explanation: The pattern is fixed by the shape of the wire and the direction by the direction of the current, so only the arrows reverse.

questions.stem: Which list correctly describes what our solar system contains?

options.text: One star, the eight planets, the dwarf planets and the planets' moons
One star and the eight planets that orbit around it, nothing else
One star, nine planets including Pluto, and the moons of those
Eight planets and their moons, with the Sun counted as a planet

questions.explanation: This is exactly the membership the specification gives: one star, the Sun, the eight planets, the dwarf planets, and the natural satellites that orbit planets.

questions.stem: A relay diagram shows a coil wound on an iron core in one circuit, and a pivoted iron armature that closes contacts in a second circuit. How does the relay work?

options.text: The current in the coil flows on through the contacts and into the second circuit
The magnetised iron core repels the armature and pushes it onto the contacts
The coil heats the armature, which bends until it touches the contacts
A small current magnetises the core, so the armature closes the contacts

questions.explanation: The coil's magnetic effect moves the armature, so a small current in one circuit switches on a separate circuit.

questions.stem: What is meant by a natural satellite?

options.text: A small rocky body that orbits the Sun directly, between the planets
A dwarf planet, which orbits the Sun beyond the eight planets
A moon: a body that orbits a planet rather than orbiting the Sun
A man-made craft kept in orbit by its engines, not gravity

questions.explanation: The specification defines natural satellites as the moons that orbit planets, and states that they are part of the solar system.

questions.stem: A long straight vertical wire carries a steady current. What is the shape of the magnetic field pattern around the wire?

options.text: Circles centred on the wire and lying in a plane at right angles to it
Straight lines that spread out from the wire, like spokes on a wheel
Straight lines running parallel to the wire along its whole length
Loops that leave one end of the wire and enter at the other end

questions.explanation: The field around a straight current-carrying wire is a set of concentric circles perpendicular to it.

options.text: From a cloud of dust and gas squeezed together by magnetism
From a huge ball of chemical fuel that was set alight in space
From a cloud of dust and gas in which fusion started at once
From a cloud of dust and gas pulled together by gravity

questions.explanation: The specification states that the Sun was formed from a cloud of dust and gas (nebula) pulled together by gravitational attraction.

questions.stem: An iron core is placed inside a solenoid that is carrying a current. What is the effect?

options.text: The solenoid begins to produce a magnetic field for the first time
The field grows stronger and stays on after the current is off
The core carries a current of its own that adds to the field
The magnetic field of the solenoid becomes considerably stronger

questions.explanation: Adding an iron core increases the strength of the magnetic field of a solenoid; the arrangement is an electromagnet.

questions.stem: Which two effects are in equilibrium in a stable star?

options.text: No effects at all, because equilibrium means no forces act on it
The inward pull of gravity and the outward push of gravity itself
The weight of the star and the upthrust of the gas around it
The gravitational collapse inwards and the expansion due to fusion energy

questions.explanation: The specification states that fusion reactions lead to an equilibrium between the gravitational collapse of a star and its expansion due to fusion energy.

questions.stem: Why does winding a wire into a solenoid increase the magnetic effect of the current?

options.text: The field of each turn points the same way inside the coil, so they add up
Winding the wire into a coil increases the current flowing in it
The coiled wire has a much larger resistance, and that strengthens the field
The turns of wire trap the field lines so that none can escape the coil

questions.explanation: Many turns contribute their fields at the same place and in the same direction, so the total field is much stronger.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how our solar system relates to the Milky Way?

options.text: The Milky Way is just another name for our own solar system
Our solar system is a small part of the Milky Way galaxy
The Milky Way galaxy holds everything in the universe
Our solar system lies at the exact centre of the Milky Way

questions.explanation: The specification states directly that our solar system is a small part of the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.stem: A student is asked to draw the magnetic field of a current-carrying solenoid, showing its direction. Which drawing is correct?

options.text: Parallel lines inside the coil and loops outside it, with no arrows on any line
Parallel arrows inside the coil that start at one end and stop at the other
Closely spaced parallel arrows inside the coil, looping outside from north to south
Circles drawn around the outside of the coil, with clockwise arrows shown

questions.explanation: Inside the coil the field is uniform and along the axis; outside, each line loops back, giving the bar-magnet shape.

questions.stem: At the start of a star's life cycle, why do fusion reactions begin?

options.text: Gravity draws the dust and gas together, heating it until nuclei fuse
The dust and gas catch fire and burn chemically, giving out the energy
Fusion starts as soon as gravity begins to draw the cloud inwards
Magnetic forces squeeze the cloud until its particles join together

questions.explanation: Gravitational attraction pulls the material of the nebula together; the compression raises the temperature and density until fusion reactions start.

questions.stem: A horizontal wire carries a current from left to right. The magnetic field between the poles is directed into the page. In which direction is the force on the wire?

options.text: Downwards, at right angles to both the field and the current
Upwards, at right angles to both the current and the field
Into the page, in the same direction as the field itself
To the right, in the same direction as the current

questions.explanation: First finger into the page and second finger to the right puts the thumb, and so the force, upwards.

questions.stem: The north pole of a magnet is pushed towards a coil that is part of a complete circuit. What does the magnetic field produced by the induced current do?

options.text: It reinforces the change, pulling the magnet deeper into the coil
It opposes the change, so it acts to repel the approaching pole
It strengthens the magnet's own field inside the coil, reinforcing it
It acts only on the coil itself and never on the magnet

questions.explanation: An induced current generates a magnetic field that opposes the original change, here the movement of the magnet towards the coil.

questions.stem: Which describes the graph of potential difference generated in the coil against time for a dynamo turning steadily?

options.text: A straight horizontal line at one constant positive value
A wave that rises and falls equally either side of the axis
A flat line held at a constant value below the axis
A series of humps that never cross below the time axis

questions.explanation: The dynamo's output rises and falls as the coil turns but never reverses direction.

questions.stem: A sound wave reaches the diaphragm of a moving-coil microphone. What happens next?

options.text: The diaphragm makes the magnet vibrate inside a coil that is fixed
The diaphragm and its coil vibrate near a magnet, inducing a current
A current in the coil makes the diaphragm vibrate and give out a sound
The magnet swings to and fro past a coil clamped firmly in place

questions.explanation: The coil moving in the magnetic field induces a potential difference that varies in step with the pressure variations.

questions.stem: Why is the core of a basic transformer made of iron?

options.text: Iron is easily magnetised by the changing field
Iron conducts an electric current better than copper
Iron carries the current across from one coil to the other
Iron does not get hot when a current flows in it

questions.explanation: Iron is used as it is easily magnetised, so it carries the changing field to the secondary coil.

questions.stem: Which change would increase the size of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?

options.text: Using much longer connecting leads between the cell and the wire
Using a much longer wire, most of it outside the field
Using a stronger magnet, so that the flux density is larger
Reducing the current so that less energy is lost as heat

questions.explanation: The force depends on the magnetic flux density, the current and the length of conductor in the field.
